thread.title: GDX: Is This Time Different? - VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF (NYSEARCA:GDX)

author: Income Generator
title: GDX: Is This Time Different? - VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF (NYSEARCA:GDX)
text:
Just as investors thought they had escaped market turmoil in the early parts of 2018 , those trends returned once again to finish the year with a vengeance . As persistent volatility levels continued to edge higher, investors returned to the precious metals sector as a key safe haven during times of crisis. As a result, the VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF ( GDX ) broke out of its massive, multi-year downtrend and rallied 10.38% in the month of December. These moves indicate the best performances we have seen in the precious metals miners in a decade and broader trends unfolding in the macro environment should continue to be supportive for long positions in GDX.
(Source: ETF.com)
The VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF is a well-diversified instrument which offers broad exposure to the world’s senior gold mining companies. The top-10 stocks held in the fund make up 57.79% of the total allocation. The most significant holdings in the fund include Barrick Gold Corp. (NYSE: GOLD ) at 11.57% of the total allocation. This is followed by Newmont Mining Corp. ( NEM ) at 8.74% and Franco-Nevada Corp. ( FNV ) at 6.33% of the allocation. The fund’s expense ratio is roughly in line with the category averages, at 0.53%
(Source: ETFdb.com)
Looking at the flow activities which have been directed toward the VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF, we can see trends which do not seem to match the widespread pessimism which had been associated with the gold mining industry for most of 2018. Over the last year, GDX has benefited from inflows of $3,623.3 million, and these bullish trends actually maintained themselves with high levels of consistency throughout the period. Over the last 26 weeks, the fund has benefited from inflows of $2,406.0 million. This trend has held right up to the most recent weekly and monthly periods, and GDX has consistently maintained its position near the top-end of its category averages for each of these time intervals.
Interestingly, this bullish activity occurred as Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies plummeted. Essentially, what this tells us is that the market has once again returned to the “tried and true” formula of precious metals asset exposure as the preferred safe haven in uncertain markets. Volatility levels continue to rise in most equity sectors, weaknesses have become apparent in the U.S. dollar, and the rippling effects of a trade war with China have conspired to undermine investor faith in the prior bull rally.
The severity of these economic concerns seems to be confirmed when companies like Apple, Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL ) release bombshell earnings warnings indicating sharp declines in expected global earnings figures. The news actually sent Apple to fourth on the list of the world’s most valuable companies, and many have suggested that this is just early evidence that a global recession could be experienced in the second half of 2019 .
(Source: Bloomberg)
Additional evidence that “this time is different” can be seen in the fact that the final weeks of the year tend to be highly bullish for equities. Typically, this is a negative for instruments like the VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF because of the inverse correlation the fund shares with benchmarks like the S&P 500. In December, the BI-Global Senior Gold Valuation Peers Index had its best year-end performance since the 2008 financial crisis (while the S&P 500 lost 9.18% for the period). Given the contrasts in historical trend activity, this sets the mining sector on a firm path to produce enhanced gains in 2019.
But there are still risks involved, and these should be assessed before establishing long positions in the VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF. In other words, it is important to look at the financial health of the largest holdings in GDX, given the multitude of difficulties which have been faced by the mining industry over the last decade. Perhaps, the best way to accomplish this is through the forward net debt-to-EBITDA ratio, which allows us to assess a company’s ability to repay its debt load. Essentially, these ratios are drawn from forward earnings and they tell us the number of years which will likely to be required in order for each gold miner to pay back its debt obligations.
(Source: Market Realist)
When we are looking at the net debt-to-EBITDA metric, lower numbers are preferred. In the figures above, we can see that Newmont Mining exhibits the most impressive net debt-to-EBITDA ratio (0.48). Newmont’s stable earnings expectations suggest strong capabilities to reduce and overcome debt levels, and the miner’s metrics have improved drastically since 2015. Unfortunately, things look less impressive for Kinross Gold ( KGC ) and Barrick Gold. But their net debt-to-EBITDA ratios (1.2 for KGC and 1.3 for ABX) are still far below the figure seen in Goldcorp ( GG ), which is currently the worst performer in the group (at 2.37). These are important factors which present an added element of risk for those considering long positions in GDX.
Fortunately, the figures indicated by net debt-to-forward EBITDA ratios can fluctuate rapidly (as they depend on the earnings estimates associated with each senior gold miner). We could start to see upside surprises in these metrics as demand for gold continues to rise and earnings expectations for the group start to show steadier improvements.
Thus far, it would seem that investors expect these trends to unfold in a favorable direction as the VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF has clearly broken out of its massive, multi-year downtrend. The fund has already moved above important resistance levels at $20.50 and this puts the July 2018 highs at $22.94 back into focus. Ultimately, these moves indicate the best performances we have seen in the precious metals miners in a decade and this should continue to bring supportive elements and drive gains for long positions in GDX.
Thank you for reading.
